question: Which section of the digestive tract can be affected by Crohn's disease?

options.B: Only the rectum and sigmoid colon
options.C: Any part from the mouth to the anus
options.D: Only the first part of the small intestine

explanation: Crohn's disease can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract and often leaves healthy areas in between, unlike other bowel conditions that stay in one fixed spot. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why is recognizing Crohn's disease early so important for patient care?

options.A: It guarantees a complete surgical cure within weeks
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future dietary changes
options.C: It prevents long-term complications like bowel obstruction
options.D: It stops patients from ever needing medication again

explanation: Catching the disease early helps control deep inflammation before it causes permanent scarring, narrowing, and blockages in the intestines. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h1)

question: What does the term 'transmural inflammation' mean in Crohn's disease?

options.A: Rapid bacterial infection localized inside the fecal stream
options.B: Inflammation limited strictly to the inner mucosal lining
options.C: Swelling that affects only the outermost serosal layer
options.D: Inflammation spreading across all layers of the bowel wall

explanation: Transmural means the inflammation goes deep, passing through every layer of the intestinal wall from the inside out. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h2)

question: What are the abnormal tissue tunnels called that can connect the bowel to the skin or other organs?
explanation: Deep ulcers in the bowel wall can tunnel straight through to nearby organs or the skin, creating abnormal connections known as fistulas. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h2)

question: Which of these symptoms is most typical of Crohn's disease?

options.A: Severe constipation alternating with projectile vomiting
options.B: Massive, painless rectal bleeding every morning
options.C: High fever with a sudden skin rash and clear watery stools
options.D: Persistent non-bloody diarrhea and right lower quadrant pain

explanation: While some conditions cause heavy bleeding, Crohn's frequently targets the end of the small intestine, leading to right lower quadrant pain and loose stools. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h3)

question: A patient with long-standing Crohn's disease reports painful red bumps on the front of both shins. What is this finding called?
explanation: Erythema nodosum describes painful, red, raised bumps typically found on the shins that can appear alongside inflammatory bowel disease. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h3)

question: What is the main clue when a colonoscopy reveals 'skip lesions'?

options.A: It indicates that the disease is completely cured
options.B: It strongly points toward a diagnosis of Crohn's disease
options.C: It shows that only the rectal mucosa is involved
options.D: It proves the infection is caused by a specific parasite

explanation: Skip lesions mean healthy tissue sits right next to inflamed tissue, which is a classic sign that helps separate Crohn's disease from continuous conditions like ulcerative colitis. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h4)

question: Why do doctors order C-reactive protein (CRP) blood tests for suspected Crohn's disease?

options.A: To detect systemic inflammation happening inside the body
options.B: To screen for specific viral infections in the liver
options.C: To check the exact level of circulating digestive enzymes
options.D: To measure how fast red blood cells settle to the bottom

explanation: CRP is a protein produced by the liver that increases rapidly when there is active inflammation anywhere in the body, including the digestive tract. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h4)

question: Which type of medication is usually given for quick relief during a severe Crohn's disease flare?
explanation: Corticosteroids calm the immune system down very quickly, making them the top choice for bringing sudden, severe flares under control. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why are corticosteroids generally avoided for long-term maintenance in Crohn's disease?

options.A: They immediately trigger severe internal bleeding
options.B: They cure the disease permanently and are no longer needed
options.C: They stop working entirely after just three days
options.D: They cause significant long-term adverse side effects

explanation: Using steroids for a long time can lead to bone thinning, weight gain, high blood sugar, and a higher chance of infection, so other drugs are preferred for daily management. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why is surgery considered a management tool rather than a permanent cure for Crohn's disease?

options.A: Inflammation frequently recurs near the surgical reconnection site
options.B: Surgical removal causes the disease to spread to the lungs
options.C: The body instantly rejects any reconnected sections of intestine
options.D: Surgeons are unable to remove all of the affected bowel tissue

explanation: Because Crohn's is a body-wide inflammatory condition, removing a blocked section solves that specific problem, but inflammation often returns later near where the bowel was reconnected. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h6)

question: Which of these is a common reason to perform surgery for a patient with Crohn's disease?

options.A: Fixed intestinal strictures causing bowel obstruction
options.B: A mild episode of transient morning nausea
options.C: Temporary fatigue during a routine work shift
options.D: A slight elevation in white blood cell count

explanation: When scar tissue creates a narrow spot that blocks stool and refuses to open up with medication, surgery is needed to clear or bypass the blockage. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why do patients who have had part of their terminal ileum removed often need vitamin B12 supplements?

options.A: B12 vitamins react negatively with routine pain medications
options.B: The terminal ileum is the specific site where B12 is absorbed
options.C: The stomach stops producing hydrochloric acid completely
options.D: Surgical incisions destroy the body's ability to store water

explanation: The terminal ileum is the exact area where vitamin B12 is absorbed into the body, so removing that section means supplements are required to prevent a deficiency. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h7)

question: What kind of diet is often recommended during an active Crohn's flare to keep the bowel calm?

options.B: A high-fat diet consisting primarily of fried foods
options.C: A strict liquid-only diet restricted to plain water
options.D: A high-fiber diet packed with raw vegetables and bran

explanation: Low-residue diets reduce the amount of roughage passing through the digestive tract, which helps decrease cramping and stool frequency when the bowel is inflamed. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h7)

question: What is the main reason for careful perianal skin care in a patient with active Crohn's disease?

options.A: To eliminate the need for taking daily oral anti-inflammatory drugs
options.B: To stimulate the normal absorption of vitamin B12 in the colon
options.C: To prevent painful skin breakdown from chronic diarrhea and drainage
options.D: To cure internal fistulas without needing any surgical procedures

explanation: Frequent watery stools and drainage from fistulas can easily irritate sensitive skin, making gentle cleaning and barrier protection an important part of nursing care. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h8)

question: Which of these points is most important when teaching a patient about maintenance medication for Crohn's disease?

options.A: Stop taking all prescription drugs as soon as abdominal pain stops
options.B: Switch to herbal remedies if the pharmacy runs out of stock
options.C: Double the medication dose whenever eating a high-fiber meal
options.D: Continue taking medications consistently even during periods of remission

explanation: Maintenance medications keep the immune system stable, so stopping them just because symptoms disappear often leads to a sudden flare-up. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h8)
